panels.description:
Torrents whose file the library shares, so seeding them costs no extra disk at all and the cleanup leaves them alone forever.

These counts plus the duplicates and whatever is still downloading are every torrent in qBittorrent: a film is in exactly one stage.

panels.title: Duplicate copies
panels.description:
Films that live on disk twice, because the release came packed in RAR: what qBittorrent seeds is 96 `.rNN` archives, and what Plex plays is the `.mkv` unpackerr extracted out of them. Two separate sets of bytes, and a hardlink cannot bridge them.

Every byte here comes back on its own: the archives are dropped the moment their tracker is paid, whether or not the film is still in the library. The extracted film is a different file and is never touched.

panels.title: These films go next
panels.description:
Every film Maintainerr has queued: watched to at least 95% of its runtime, and more than two days ago. This is the same list as the `Pending deletion` collection in Plex.

They are deleted on the next handler run, which is 00:00 and 12:00. The library copy goes and the film is unmonitored in Radarr; the torrent stays seeding until its tracker is paid.

To save one, exclude it in Maintainerr (`https://maintainerr.platanosverdes.com`) or postpone it there. Marking a film as watched by hand puts it here too: Plex writes the same flags whether you watched it or clicked the button.

panels.title: Trackers
panels.description:
Every tracker with a torrent here, and the goal the cleanup applies to it. Public ones ask nothing: their torrents go as soon as the film leaves the library. Private goals come from config/qbittorrent/seed-rules.json, and either the hours or the ratio clears the debt, whichever lands first.

Sorted by what it asks for, so private trackers come first: those are the ones whose rules you can actually break. Biggest first within each group.

panels.title: Seed progress
panels.description:
How far each waiting film is along its tracker's goal. Either the hours or the ratio clears the debt, so this is whichever is further along: a torrent at 20% of the hours and 80% of the ratio is 80% done.

At 100% the next hourly pass deletes it. Remember qBittorrent only counts time spent actually seeding, so a queued torrent stands still.
